scope: Parent qualitative assessment against six treatments approved by Ashley before fresh judging; not an independent human score or automatic text-match metric.

rubric.pass: Follows the agreed treatment and preserves required information.
rubric.partial: Correct consolidation direction but omits a required merge/preservation step.
rubric.fail: Rejects the agreed consolidation or proposes an incompatible treatment.

a.reason: Flags overlap and shortens/links, but leaves enterprise/update/signing/cross-platform additions on the route page conditionally rather than explicitly merging useful general additions into the builder guide. Correctly flags capability scope for verification.

b.reason: Calls the passages distinct and proposes no consolidation.

a.reason: Consolidates the custom-connector and Inspector instructions, but explicitly leaves the unique Claude Code check in the index rather than incorporating it into the testing guide.

b.reason: Consolidates the custom-connector and Inspector instructions, but explicitly retains the Claude Code command and /mcp note in the index rather than moving them into the testing guide.

a.reason: Moves detailed matching explanation to the external-links guide while retaining optional-field, applicability, and ownership requirements locally; calls for reconciliation before editing.

b.reason: Makes external-links the reference and retains submission ownership and optional-field requirements, with accepted-form verification before editing.

a.reason: Keeps security warnings visible in both independent procedures and recognizes their distinct cleanup/rationale.

b.reason: Keeps both warnings and their local cleanup/security details.

a.reason: Keeps detailed preparation guidance and the short prerequisite in the checklist.

b.reason: Keeps the populated-account prerequisite visible in both contexts.

a.reason: Keeps service-specific organization/administrator prerequisites distinct from the generic user flow.

b.reason: Keeps Microsoft tenant/role prerequisites and generic authentication distinct.
